newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets dumping probe procedures - paper.
newsitem.headline: China sets dumping probe procedures - paper.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it had set up a system to investigate complaints of unfair competition from imports and impose countervailing duties.

The International Business Daily quoted the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying that it would accept and investigate complaints from domestic companies of unfair pricing from imports.

The ministry issued a statement advising domestic companies where to file and how to document their complaints. It also said those companies defending themselves against such complaints should provide sales and pricing data.
The newspaper, which is published by the ministry, said some foreign companies had used unfair prices to capture a share of the domestic market.

This had forced many Chinese manufacturers out of the market or to the brink of bankruptcy, it said, adding that the dumping of imported goods was costing China some 10 billion yuan ($1.2 billion) a year and had already caused the loss of hundreds of thousands of jobs.
Many domestic manufacturers already were pressuring the government to take steps to offset these practices, it said.

Under China's foreign trade law, Beijing can take "appropriate measures" to reduce or eliminate damage or potential damage to domestic manufacturers from imports that are priced "below normal levels".

The newspaper did not give criteria for determining whether domestic companies had been hurt or could be hurt by imports, although it said the ministry would evaluate sales, production, employment, operating rates and profits of companies filing complaints.
The domestic media have said Beijing was drafting anti-dumping laws to protect domestic industry from unfair foreign competition.
